set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/personal-task-manager-262972-262981/to_do_app_native"
mkdir -p "$WS/test" "$WS/cmake" && cd "$WS"
cat > "$WS/test/test_example.cpp" <<'CPP'
#define CATCH_CONFIG_MAIN
#include <catch2/catch.hpp>
TEST_CASE("sanity") { REQUIRE(1==1); }
CPP
cat > "$WS/cmake/tests.cmake" <<'CM'
# generated tests fragment - creates a test target and registers with CTest
enable_testing()
add_executable(tests test/test_example.cpp)
if(TARGET PkgConfig::GTK4)
  target_link_libraries(tests PRIVATE PkgConfig::GTK4)
elseif(GTK4_FOUND)
  target_include_directories(tests PRIVATE ${GTK4_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  target_link_libraries(tests PRIVATE ${GTK4_LIBRARIES})
endif()
add_test(NAME sanity COMMAND $<TARGET_FILE:tests>)
add_custom_target(run-tests COMMAND $<TARGET_FILE:tests> DEPENDS tests)
CM

Wait for the pidfile, validate the process is alive, and write a basic runtime check file. Uses DISPLAY=:99 by default. steps.name: validation - build, start, run tests, and stop scaffolded app
steps.description: Comprehensive validation: builds the project (reuses build step), starts the GUI, runs CTest from the build dir, captures ctest exit code, collects cmake/gcc versions and logs into validation_evidence.txt, then stops the app cleanly by signalling the recorded PID/process group. Operates in workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/personal-task-manager-262972-262981/to_do_app_native.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/personal-task-manager-262972-262981/to_do_app_native"
EVID="$WS/validation_evidence.txt"
: > "$EVID"
cd "$WS"
cmake --version >> "$EVID" 2>&1 || true
g++ --version | head -n1 >> "$EVID" 2>&1 || true
# Build
"$WS/build.sh"
# Start
export DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-:99}
"$WS/start-wrapper.sh"
PIDFILE="$WS/.app_pid"
for i in $(seq 1 30); do if [ -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then break; fi; sleep 1; done
if [ ! -f "$PIDFILE" ]; then echo 'app failed to start (no pid file)' >> "$EVID"; exit 3; fi
APP_PID=$(cat "$PIDFILE")
printf "app_pid=%s\n" "$APP_PID" >> "$EVID"
# brief wait for UI init
sleep 2
# Run tests via CTest from build dir, capture exit code correctly
cd "$WS/build"
TEST_RESULT=0
ctest --output-on-failure -C Debug || TEST_RESULT=$?
printf "ctest_exit=%s\n" "$TEST_RESULT" >> "$EVID"
# capture direct test binary if present
TEST_BIN=$(find "$WS/build" -type f -executable -name tests -print -quit || true)
if [ -n "$TEST_BIN" ]; then "$TEST_BIN" > "$WS/logs/tests.out" 2>&1 || true; echo "tests_log=$WS/logs/tests.out" >> "$EVID"; fi
echo "app_log=$WS/logs/app.log" >> "$EVID"
# Stop app
if [ -n "$APP_PID" ] && ps -p "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p "$APP_PID" | tr -d ' ' || true)
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 3; if ps -p "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill -KILL -"$PGID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  else kill -TERM "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 2; kill -KILL "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
  rm -f "$PIDFILE" || true
fi
if ps -p "$APP_PID" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'failed to stop app' >> "$EVID"; exit 6; fi
echo "validation: success" >> "$EVID"

This guarantees the build step no longer fails due to a missing build script. I preserved existing working steps (env-001, scaffold-001, test-001, validation-001, start-001) and modified only build-001 to make it self-healing: if the workspace lacks build.sh the build step will generate the canonical build.sh (matching the scaffold plan) and make it executable before invoking it. This keeps steps atomic, fail-fast, and idempotent. All scripts use the authoritative workspace path, are non-interactive, include set -euo pipefail, use sudo when needed, and minimize output. The plan remains small (6 steps) and satisfies the requirements for a headless GTK4 C++ development environment with single-header Catch2 testing. The change resolves the engineer's critical blocking issue by guaranteeing the presence and executability of build.sh prior to attempting the build.
